Variants.Content: Signed in 205 BC at Phoenice in Epirus, the Peace of Phoenice brought an end to the First Macedonian War. The treaty recognized minor territorial gains for Philip V in Illyria while ensuring that Macedonian fleets would never cross the Adriatic to aid Hannibal. This diplomatic success neutralized Rome's eastern flank, freeing all strategic resources for Scipio's climactic African campaign.
